_readme: THE declared answer to 'what writes this bus file'. bus-vocabulary-drift.py reads
producers from THIS FILE AND NOTHING ELSE. There is no prose inference left in the
detector: no write-verb regex, no '## Writes' scrape, no {{BUS_DIR}} path match.
WHY (ASK-885, successor to ASK-874 PR #202 which was closed after six review rounds):
the detector used to infer producers from agent prompt prose. Five successive
definitions of 'produced' were each wrong in a different direction -- membership in a
map, every *.json, {{BUS_DIR}}-qualified only, {{BUS_DIR}}+write-verb (which counted
READS as writes), and the union with '## Writes' (which read a prohibited
q-system/memory/ write as a bus artifact). Every fix uncovered a convention nobody
knew existed, because prose has no schema to check you. This file is the schema.
DESIGN OPTIONS CONSIDERED, and why this one (the DoR asked for the fork to be named,
not picked silently):
a) a `produces:` key in agent frontmatter -- rejected. 6 of the bus files come from
SCRIPTS the orchestrator shells out to (compliance.json via compliance-check.py
and five more below). Those have no agent file to carry frontmatter, so this
option cannot express the majority case and would leave the detector inferring.
b) a '## Writes' section on step-orchestrator.md keyed by script -- rejected. It is
markdown, so it reintroduces exactly the failure this issue exists to end: a
heading convention with no schema, checkable only by a regex that has already
been wrong five times.
c) THIS FILE: one JSON manifest, one schema, agents and scripts expressed the same
way. PICKED. It is the only option where the declaration is machine-checkable
and where an agent-produced and a script-produced file are the same kind of row.
THE MANIFEST IS CHECKED, NOT TRUSTED. Every `source` below names a real path relative
to the repo root, and the detector emits a `producer-source-missing` finding for any
source file that does not exist. A manifest nobody validates is prose in a .json hat.
WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT DO, said out loud rather than left for the next reviewer: it
cannot prove a listed source ACTUALLY writes the file at runtime, only that the file
it names exists. Adding a producer here without doing that write is a lie no checker
in this repo catches. Every row below was verified by reading the named source on
2026-08-17 (the agents' write lines, the scripts' `output_path` assignments).
Bus filenames a verifier or the bridge knows about that NOTHING in this pipeline
writes. Listed so their absence from `producers` reads as a decision rather than an
oversight. The detector does NOT read this block as a producer -- these still surface
as required-without-producer findings, which is the whole point.
not_produced.energy.json: Required at phase 0 by both verifiers. No agent and no script writes it. Phase 0 cannot pass on a real run; the suite is green only because the test fixture writes the file itself.
not_produced.dp-pipeline.json: Required at phase 3 by the MCP bus_verifier. No producer exists anywhere in the pipeline.
not_produced.tl-content.json: Promoted from optional to REQUIRED at phase 4 on Tuesdays and Thursdays, by _cadence-config.json AND by hardcoded literals in both verifiers. No producer exists, so phase 4 cannot pass two days a week.
not_produced.notion.json: 01-notion-pull.md exists and writes it, but the orchestrator dispatches `crm -> 01-crm-pull` and never dispatches 01-notion-pull (step-orchestrator.md:107). Declaring it here would assert a producer that never runs. Retiring the orphaned agent is a live-pipeline change tracked separately (ASK-874).

not_bus_files._readme: Written by pipeline members but NOT bus artifacts. Here so a future reader does not re-add them as producers, which is the exact false positive that closed ASK-874 PR #202.
not_bus_files.sycophancy-log.json: {{QROOT}}/memory/sycophancy-log.json. 06-sycophancy-audit.md is explicitly PROHIBITED from writing it (sycophancy-harness.py is the single writer). Reading its '## Writes' mention as a bus producer was a shipped false positive.
